case_title: State (NCT of Delhi) & Apex FinTech v. Zenith Cloud Technologies

contentious_issues.title: Maintainability of Criminal FIR 0412/2024 in a Commercial Contractual Dispute with Arbitration
contentious_issues.statutory_matrix: Section 482 CrPC / Section 528 BNSS vs Section 406/420 IPC
contentious_issues.prosecution_doctrine: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (1992) - Allegations disclose fraudulent inducement at inception and forgery of escrow certificate #CG-8829, which cannot be stifled under inherent powers.
contentious_issues.defense_doctrine: Dalip Kaur v. Jagnar Singh (2009) & Indian Oil Corp. v. NEPC India Ltd. (2006) - Pure commercial milestone dispute arising out of Clause 3 & 18 cannot be converted into criminal prosecution to exert pressure.

contentious_issues.title: Admissibility of Digital Server Logs and Electronic WhatsApp Transcripts Lacking 65B Certification
contentious_issues.statutory_matrix: Section 65B(4) Indian Evidence Act / Section 63(4) Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam
contentious_issues.prosecution_doctrine: State of Karnataka v. T. Naseer (2023) - Defect in Section 65B certificate is curable during trial stage before charge framing.
contentious_issues.defense_doctrine: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal (2020) 7 SCC 1 - Production of certificate under Section 65B(4) is a mandatory condition precedent for electronic record admissibility.

contentious_issues.title: Establishment of Dishonest Mens Rea at Inception for Cheating under Section 420 IPC / 318 BNS
contentious_issues.statutory_matrix: Section 415/420 Indian Penal Code / Section 316/318 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
contentious_issues.prosecution_doctrine: Ram Biraji Devi v. Umesh Kumar Singh (2006) - False representation regarding security audit certificate establishes fraudulent intent from inception.
contentious_issues.defense_doctrine: Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma v. State of Bihar (2000) 4 SCC 168 - Distinction between mere breach of contract and cheating depends on fraudulent intention at the very beginning of the transaction.
